problemStatement: Feature-branch mode needs a small live run against the real repository to exercise branch-only descendants. A root, two siblings, and one nested descendant provide that topology without changing application behavior.
solutionSummary: Create a concise three-page feature-branch field guide. The root adds a push check limited to this sample's branches, so descendants can publish without PRs. Two siblings write separate pages; a nested fourth patch extends the integration page. The local feature-branch supervisor integrates descendant branches and leaves the sole root PR for review.
currentStateAnalysis: Target main is 4baa2e8a7b4b38cfd58e2681ad3479324c5d4ce7. docs/design contains focused Markdown design notes. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs push CI on main only, so the root must establish sample-scoped push checks before descendants publish. The new mode is implemented in the invoking checkout's binary and has passed local tests.

operationalConsiderations.externalSystemAccess: The existing authenticated GitHub/SSH transports publish sample branches and create the root PR. Patch 1 creates a GitHub Actions workflow scoped to feature-branch-sample-20261002/patch-*; no new secrets or external services are introduced.
operationalConsiderations.crossRuntimeContracts: The JSON is consumed by the local onton binary. GitHub Actions attaches the sample check to each pushed commit; the supervisor reads that exact SHA. No persisted application or API format is changed.
operationalConsiderations.failureBehavior: Missing, failed, or pending branch checks hold descendant integration. The documented Git conflict/retry/dirty-checkout behavior remains owned by the supervisor. The new workflow fails on whitespace errors or a missing root guide and has a three-minute timeout.
operationalConsiderations.concurrencyAndIdempotency: Patches 2 and 3 write disjoint Markdown files; patch 4 depends on patch 3 and is the only later writer of its file. The supervisor serializes root writes and recognizes already-contained heads. Workflow concurrency cancels older runs for the same ref.
operationalConsiderations.rollbackStrategy: The sample writes Markdown and a workflow only. Revert the root PR as one unit if it is later merged; no data migration or compensating application writes are needed. Root automerge is disabled for this run.

mergabilityStrategy.featureFlagStrategy: No product flag: documentation and a workflow limited to an explicit sample branch prefix do not change application behavior. The execution mode is activated with --feature-branch.
mergabilityStrategy.patchOrderingStrategy: All four patches are INFRA. Patch 1 is the sole root, patches 2 and 3 depend on 1, and patch 4 depends on 3. Parallel writers have exclusive files.

requiredChanges.description: Checks on this sample's exact branch heads

The checks guide states that descendants publish branches without PRs, checks are attached to the exact branch HEAD, at least one check is required and all must pass, push-triggered workflows are required, integration is immediate, and the per-patch automerge toggle can pause a descendant.

The integration guide explains direct intermediate bases, the root terminal boundary, normal no-ff Git integration, normal root pushes, temporary worktrees, the shared root-write lock, and descendant rebasing. It shows patch 4 based on patch 3 until patch 3 integrates and then based on patch 1, never main.

The integration guide gains a Recovery and review section explaining dirty/diverged root checkout refusal, idempotent already-contained heads, conflict routing to the descendant, retry backoff and cap, invalidation of root readiness after every update, and root promotion only after all descendants integrate and fresh current-head checks pass. It links to the root and checks guides with correct relative links.

patches.title: Add sample root guide and scoped push checks

files.description: Checks on this sample's exact branch heads

changes: This is a live feature-branch-mode smoke run, limited to documentation and a sample-scoped CI workflow. The supervisor is the locally built feature-branch binary; the target main branch does not need to contain that binary. Do not change application logic, existing CI, or files outside this patch's declared frame. Commit your completed patch; the supervisor owns publishing and PR creation. Do not enable root automerge or merge anything into main.

Create docs/design/feature-branch-sample.md as a concise field guide covering the contract in the spec; add relative links to feature-branch-checks.md and feature-branch-integration.md, which descendant patches will create.

Create .github/workflows/feature-branch-sample.yml with name "Feature branch sample", push branches ["feature-branch-sample-20261002/patch-*"], and pull_request targeting main filtered to docs/design/feature-branch-*.md and this workflow file. Use contents: read, ubuntu-latest, timeout-minutes: 3, and concurrency grouped by workflow/ref with cancel-in-progress: true. One job named "Feature branch sample checks" uses actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 with fetch-depth: 2 and runs git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD plus test -s docs/design/feature-branch-sample.md. This is a lightweight source-hygiene check; existing PR CI remains the repository correctness gate. Do not edit .github/workflows/ci.yml.
Validate workflow YAML and git diff --check, then run the repository build/test/format gate. Keep the root PR draft; the supervisor owns promotion.
